page.layout: One page of text: a centred title block at the top (author's name, subtitle in italic, then "Liber Secundus."), followed by a verse poem in italic running to the foot of the page. The catchword "Regia" sits at the lower right below the last line.

l.i: Nob: Rom: Columbeidos,

main_text.l: ETiam fama nouis totam terroribus urbem
Concutit, atque animos stimulis ingentibus urget,

l.i: Illa volans, grauidas ignoto milite naues,
Aeratasque virûm turmas praetexere littus
Detulit, & curuo Quinqueiae insidere portu,
Iamque armis in Regna rucent, iam templa domosque
Diripiunt, ipsumque petent in vincula Regem.
Talia per trepidas rerum miracula gentes
Monstrum immane canit, succensaque pectora bello
Inferrum vocat, attonita discurritur Urbe,
Pars fudibus, pars lethiferis armata sagittis,
Saxa gerunt pars magna, venenatasque macanas
Omnibus ora niger tingit color omnibus haerent
Indigetum fronti simulacra impressa Cemorum;
Non aliter si nocte domos immissa potentum
Flamma voret tota serpentem extinguere pestem
Urbe ruant temere cives, pars flumina plenis
Subuectare urnis, pars alta euellere tecta
Caussam igni, resonat magnis clamoribus aether
Et violata nigro pallent astra aurea fumo.
Primus adest, iaculisque manum letalibus armat

page.notes: The poem's first capital E is a large initial joined to "Tiam". The word "rucent" is printed as shown and may be a misprint for "ruent"; left as printed. "Inferrum" is printed as shown.
